story: This infrared view from the VISTA survey telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile shows Messier 55, a globular star cluster in the constellation Sagittarius, the Archer. This vast ball of ancient stars lies about 17 000 light-years from Earth.

A globular cluster is a dense, roughly spherical group of stars bound together by gravity. Its stars are typically very old, formed early in the history of their galaxy, which makes clusters like this valuable records of the distant past.

VISTA is a survey telescope, built to map large areas of sky, and it works in infrared light. Infrared passes through interstellar dust more easily than visible light and is especially good at picking up cooler stars, so an infrared view of a cluster can look quite different from a visible-light one.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (17.05 x 17.05 arcminutes) and distance (17000 light years), the frame spans roughly 84 × 84 light-years. Its light set out about 17,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is an infrared image from the VIRCAM camera on ESO's VISTA telescope, using Y and H filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.

explore: The image combines two infrared filters, Y and H, from VISTA's camera, VIRCAM, and covers a field about 17 arcminutes across. VISTA's full name is the Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy.
